steps.name: What it covers
steps.meaning: The parts that have a curve, their share of the value, and what has none yet
steps.fact: 2 parts with a curve · 75 % of the value · 4 without one yet
paragraphs: Flood on batteries: conservative entry policy (replace once water is above 0.30 m) for battery enclosures, plus the Flood Solar inverter curve reused for the separate PCS; unit values from market cost shares of the fixed Hazard reference budget. It names 2 parts: Battery enclosure (active hardware) and Separate PCS. Outside its scope: collector station and export line, autonomous internal failures (not caused by the flood) and business interruption. Kinds of damage it does not include: wave impact, scour and debris.

For this hazard the battery plant is split into 2 parts: Battery enclosure (active hardware) and Separate PCS. Parts of the plant's value with no curve yet: enclosure racks and fire suppression, electrical balance including unit transformers and cables, civil works and unallocated fieldwork.

$82.5M of $109.8M of the reference plant has a curve (75 %). No curve yet for enclosure racks and fire suppression, electrical balance (unit transformers, cables), civil works and unallocated fieldwork (25 % of the value).

steps.name: How damage is worked out
steps.meaning: How the hazard is measured, the shape of the curve, and the site adjustments
steps.fact: water depth above local grade → a step + a line through points
paragraphs: Damage is read against water depth above local grade (m). The curves take 2 forms: an on/off step: nothing, then full replacement; a line through fixed points (piecewise linear). The input, in the catalogue's words: water depth above local grade (m), finite and 0 or more; water type must be stated as fresh or saline; the PCS freshwater curve reads depth above the assumed 0.30 m entry (0 to 2 m knots, flat at full replacement beyond 0.6 m).
The seven-step audit is written in the dossier with 7 rows. A site-condition adapter has not been written for this cell.
